headline: 414 garment factories shut amid wage protests; owners to reopen today
summary: Garment manufacturers appealed to the home ministry for security as unrest entered its third day, forcing hundreds of factories to close. A newly formed wage board is set to discuss new pay structures.
details: Amid ongoing garment worker protests demanding higher wages, apparel manufacturers urged the home ministry to ensure security and restore normalcy in industrial zones. The unrest entered its third consecutive day, forcing 414 factories to remain closed, according to Industrial Police data.

Leaders from the BGMEA and BKMEA made this appeal during an emergency meeting with Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed. They briefed the minister on the situation across major industrial areas like Mirpur, Ashulia, Gazipur, Savar, and Narayanganj.

The government formed a six-member wage board on Sunday to fix the minimum monthly salary for over four million garment workers. Babul Akhter, the newly appointed workers’ representative on the board, urged protesters yesterday to return to work.

Akhter stated that the board would meet today or tomorrow to discuss the wage structure, which must take effect from December 1 under the amended Labour Act of 2026. He attributed the unrest to "outsiders," asserting that further protests were unjustified after the board's formation.

A group of trade union leaders also met the home minister, who urged them to persuade workers to end their agitation. Nazma Akter, president of Sommilito Garments Sramik Federation, called the continued unrest illogical, emphasizing the board's need for time to finalize recommendations.

Manufacturers expressed concerns over production delays, shipment disruptions, costly air freight, and cancellation of work orders due to the unrest. BGMEA Vice-President Rezwan Selim confirmed the home minister's suggestion to reopen factories today.

BKMEA President Mohammad Hatem alleged that the unrest was no longer about wages but was being fueled by outsiders seeking to destabilize the industry. The home minister echoed this, claiming opportunists and supporters of "fascist forces" had infiltrated the protests.

The minister warned that those responsible for disorder would be identified and brought to justice, citing CCTV footage analysis. He also mentioned that the government would consider the lawful release of innocent workers and labour leaders arrested, following the Prime Minister's instructions for a fair minimum wage.
caption:
Over 400 garment factories in Bangladesh were forced to close amid ongoing worker protests demanding higher wages for a third consecutive day.

headline_marked: ICT prosecution [[charges 7 Awami League leaders]] for July uprising crimes
headline: ICT prosecution charges 7 Awami League leaders for July uprising crimes
summary: The formal charge was submitted to the International Crimes Tribunal, alleging their involvement in planning and implementing a state policy to suppress the 2024 July uprising. Six of the accused are currently in jail.
details: The prosecution has formally submitted charges to the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) against seven Awami League leaders. These charges relate to alleged crimes against humanity during the July uprising in 2024.

The accused include former ministers Amir Hossain Amu, Abdur Razzaque, Shahjahan Khan, Dipu Moni, Mirza Azam, and Faruk Khan, along with former prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s energy adviser Taufiq-e-Elahi Chowdhury. Six of them are currently in jail, while Mirza Azam remains absconding.

Prosecutor Gazi Monawar Hossain Tamim stated that the accused allegedly helped plan, facilitate, and implement a state policy to suppress the uprising. The then government reportedly adopted the suppression of the movement as state policy.

The Awami League and the 14-party alliance also allegedly made political decisions to crush the movement. The accused, as influential members and policymakers, are said to have participated in and contributed to the crackdown.

Evidence submitted by the prosecution includes recordings of conversations involving Sheikh Hasina and the accused, as well as the United Nations fact-finding report on the July uprising. The charge will be presented before the tribunal for a hearing at a later date.
